items.title: Robotics roadmaps from around the world spotlight of the month: China
items.summary: China is prioritizing embodied AI and humanoid robotics to achieve industrial and geopolitical dominance, leveraging its manufacturing base and state-orchestrated Five-Year Plans. These plans drove the robotics sector, leading to significant increases in domestic industrial robot market share and global installation quantities by 2025. A critical bottleneck remains in precision hardware and semiconductor self-sufficiency, as reliance on foreign components hinders full autonomy. The 15th Five-Year Plan is shifting focus to embodied AI, heavily subsidizing humanoid development to drive physical AI and data aggregation. This strategy involves a high-risk gamble on humanoids, balancing rapid development with the risk of market overcapacity and structural instability.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "Robotics roadmaps from around the world spotlight of the month: China" details China's strategic focus on embodied artificial intelligence and humanoid robotics to achieve industrial and geopolitical dominance. This focus has driven significant increases in domestic industrial robot market share and global installation quantities by 2025 through state-orchestrated Five-Year Plans. The 15th Five-Year Plan is currently shifting emphasis toward embodied AI, heavily subsidizing humanoid development to advance physical AI and data aggregation. This strategy involves a high-risk commitment to humanoid development while balancing rapid progress against potential market overcapacity and structural instability. A critical bottleneck identified is the necessity for precision hardware and semiconductor self-sufficiency, as continued reliance on foreign components impedes full autonomy. The industry should monitor the trajectory of these state-driven development pathways for future technological shifts.

items.title: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 Advances Agentic, Open Source Robotics Development
items.summary: NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 introduces GPU-accelerated packages and agentic workflows to accelerate the development and deployment of robotics applications. It integrates NVIDIA accelerated computing, physical AI models, and production-ready libraries into the open-source ROS framework. This release provides agent-ready skills, such as FoundationPose for faster object perception and agent-ready pick and place workflows. The update supports the latest ROS platforms and leverages CUDA for efficient GPU acceleration across different hardware. It enables the combination of an open robotics ecosystem with accelerated computing to build capable physical AI systems.

items.title: Accelerating a ROS 2 Node with an AI Agent and NVIDIA Isaac ROS
items.summary: ROS 2 nodes can now exchange GPU-resident payloads via zero-copy transport using the `rosidl::Buffer` and the NVIDIA CUDA buffer backend. This backend allows for efficient data movement between nodes without serialization or host copies when runtime conditions permit. An AI coding agent, using the `migrate-node-to-rosidl-buffer` skill, automates the process of auditing, refactoring, and verifying this migration in CUDA-accelerated nodes. The process demonstrated on a Depth Anything 3 node involves updating data handling to use CUDA buffers for direct inference results. This enables faster, more efficient data pipelines in robotics applications on platforms like NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor.
items.audio_script: From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Accelerating a ROS 2 Node with an AI Agent and NVIDIA Isaac ROS" details how ROS 2 nodes can now exchange GPU-resident payloads via zero-copy transport utilizing the rosidl::Buffer and the NVIDIA CUDA buffer backend. This backend facilitates efficient data movement between nodes without requiring serialization or host copies when runtime conditions are favorable. An AI coding agent, employing the migrate-node-to-rosidl-buffer skill, automates the auditing, refactoring, and verification of this migration within CUDA-accelerated nodes. The demonstration involved updating data handling within a Depth Anything 3 node to leverage CUDA buffers for direct inference results, leading to faster and more efficient data pipelines in robotics applications running on platforms such as the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor. This development indicates a pathway for significantly accelerating data processing in real-time robotic systems.

items.title: Barbara Mazzolai Wants to Build a New Field of Robotics
items.summary: Barbara Mazzolai seeks to establish a new field of research called "sustainability robotics" by integrating environmental responsibility into robot design. She draws inspiration from nature, using biological models like octopuses and plant roots to develop innovative robotic systems. Her vision emphasizes reducing technological footprints and ensuring robots are symbiotic with both humanity and nature. Key to her approach is incorporating a life cycle perspective so robots can be reused, recycled, or biodegraded. Mazzolai aims to inspire future roboticists to develop technology that actively helps mitigate environmental damage.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, Barbara Mazzolai Wants to Build a New Field of Robotics. This report details the proposal for a new research field termed sustainability robotics, which integrates environmental responsibility into robot design by drawing inspiration from biological models. The research involves developing innovative robotic systems by utilizing biological models such as octopuses and plant roots. This approach emphasizes reducing technological footprints and establishing a life cycle perspective allowing robots to be reused, recycled, or biodegraded. The methodology centers on ensuring robots are symbiotic with both humanity and nature to actively mitigate environmental damage. This work aims to inspire future roboticists in developing environmentally conscious technology. The focus signals a shift towards ecologically integrated engineering within the robotics domain.

items.title: Towards Adaptive Interaction Strategies for Human Companion Robot via Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The study proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) strategy to enable mobile human-companion robots to dynamically adjust their tracking positions in real-world environments. This method addresses the limitations of traditional methods that restrict robots to fixed relative positions. A human-robot companion controller is developed by integrating Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control with Control Barrier Functions (CBF) for safe and accurate following. Experiments demonstrated that the proposed approach improved tracking accuracy and success rates by 24% and 47%, respectively, while enhancing human comfort. The robot successfully accompanied a person walking at speeds up to 1.7 m/s while respecting intimate space and obstacles.

items.title: Cosserat Modeling of Trimmed Helicoid Soft Arms with a Separated-Section Constitutive Law
items.summary: This paper formulates a separated-section constitutive law for cosserat rod models of trimmed helicoid soft arms. It addresses the inaccuracy of standard models for these arms by accounting for separated load-bearing helix domains connected by sparse fused crossings. The model captures compliance from relative motion between domains, resulting in a strongly anisotropic effective sectional stiffness. This law is integrated into a geometrically exact dynamic Cosserat model suitable for rapid planning and control in soft robots. Experimental results show small position errors across measured configurations.

items.title: Learning to Plan in Human-Robot Collaboration: Multimodal Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Interaction
items.summary: The paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL) approach to automatically generate multimodal policies for robot assistants in human-robot collaboration. The system focuses on a scenario where a robot assists a user in object location by managing language and physical action signals. The agent is trained using a simulator incorporating human data and a simple reward function. Human study results show the system demonstrates high usability and effective task completion in real-world settings. This method offers a scalable alternative for designing interaction managers in multimodal collaborations.

items.title: JAMB: Joint Action-Motion Diffusion for Bimanual Manipulation
items.summary: Coordinated bimanual manipulation is challenging because arm motions affect the shared 3D scene. JAMB proposes a diffusion policy that jointly denoises bimanual actions and future 3D point tracks. It achieves this by evolving action and track hypotheses together within a shared Transformer. The method grounds multimodal representations in a shared spatiotemporal coordinate system for geometry-aware interaction. JAMB significantly outperforms baselines across simulation and real-world bimanual manipulation tasks.

items.title: GINIO: A Geometric SO(3)-Equivariant Interface for Neural Inertial Odometry
items.summary: GINIO introduces a geometric SO(3)-equivariant interface for neural inertial odometry to handle arbitrary IMU frame rotations. The framework ensures that motion measurements and uncertainties transform consistently according to tensorial laws. It includes Last-Frame Alignment (LFA) for efficient sensor-frame learning and a connected estimator to track nuisance parameters. Experiments show GINIO achieves superior performance in various benchmarks, significantly reducing absolute time error and covariance-equivariance error compared to other methods.

items.title: Learning from Humans for Proactive Assistance in Human-Robot Collaborative Transport
items.summary: The research focuses on human-robot collaborative transport, where a robot assists a human in moving objects. The key insight is that obstacle-constrained transport requires integrating predictions of human behavior with compliant robot control. The PROACT framework uses a transformer architecture trained on human transport demonstrations to predict future object motion. This approach resulted in significant reductions in interaction work and completion time compared to baseline methods. PROACT achieved a 59.2\% reduction in interaction work and a 12.9\% reduction in completion time in experiments.

items.title: HOTICE: Whole-Body Humanoid Object Transportation in Cluttered Environments
items.summary: HOTICE is a whole-body humanoid learning framework designed for transporting objects in cluttered environments. It introduces Humanoid-Object Decoupled Potential Fields to guide collision-avoidance for both the robot and the payload. A dual-agent reinforcement learning architecture is used to manage the large action space by decoupling upper- and lower-body control while maintaining whole-body coordination. A specialist-to-generalist distillation strategy is employed to train a policy that generalizes across diverse cluttered scenes. Evaluations in simulation and on a real humanoid demonstrate effective and robust object transportation in complex settings.

items.title: Capability-Aware Arbitration for Semantic Intent-Based Shared Control
items.summary: Shared control frameworks often over-help due to overconfidence in inferred human intent. This work proposes a capability-aware framework to mitigate this by combining semantic-intent confidence from a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) capability confidence. The VLA capability confidence is estimated online from the dispersion and instability of stochastic action trajectories. A nonlinear arbitration policy merges these two confidence measures using a sigmoid mapping to adjust robot authority. Evaluation showed this method achieved the highest task success rate (92%) and improved control friendliness compared to other shared-control methods.
